title: How Casper's Manifest Plans to Capture the $16T Tokenized Asset Industry
partialText:
In Zug today, the Casper Association published the Casper Manifest, a multi-year technical roadmap that the network is positioning as its bet on what the next cycle of blockchain infrastructure will actually be used for. The document was introduced by Casper Association President and CTO Michael Steuer at the Bermuda Digital Finance Forum, the invitation-only 500-person event co-hosted by SALT and Penrose Partners at the Hamilton Princess, in front of an audience of Web3 protocols, traditional finance, and institutional finance leaders. The Manifest commits the network to nine coordinated protocol initiatives, with the first, X402 micropayments, shipping in the next few weeks.

https://x.com/Casper_Network/status/2054191576608330164?embedable=true

\ The Manifest commits the network to nine coordinated protocol initiatives, with the first, X402 micropayments, shipping in the next few weeks.

\

The framing is unusual for the category. Most Layer 1 roadmaps in 2026 emphasize throughput, fees, or ecosystem incentives. The Casper Manifest emphasizes none of those. The nine initiatives are organized around three audiences the network is now explicitly building for: developers shipping regulated assets, end-users who should never see a private key, and AI agents that need to pay for compute and data without a human in the loop.

\ WHAT THE NINE INITIATIVES ACTUALLY DO

The Manifest groups its nine initiatives into six areas. EVM compatibility brings Solidity, MetaMask, and Ethereum's smart-contract libraries onto Casper's WebAssembly foundation, with a native token registry that prevents fragmentation between the two execution environments.

\

Frictionless UX delivers gasless transactions, batch operations, and smart accounts with biometric authentication, so an end-user signs in with a fingerprint rather than managing keys. Compliance and privacy as one system ships compliant security tokens aligned with the ERC-3643 standard, alongside a multi-phase privacy roadmap that produces confidential transactions with fixed costs and built-in tools for auditors and regulators.

\ Machine-economy infrastructure implements the X402 open payment standard, enabling AI agents to pay each other over HTTP in stablecoins, with scoped spending permissions inherited from the same smart accounts built for humans. First-class native tokens elevate every user-created token to protocol-level status with the same fixed costs as native transfers. Quantum-safe cryptography ships hybrid accounts carrying both classical and post-quantum keys during a transition period.

\

Read together, the nine initiatives describe a network optimized for two things at once: tokenizing regulated assets and routing autonomous machine payments. Those are the two largest greenfield demand sources for blockchain infrastructure in 2026, and they happen to be the two areas where the existing Layer 1 stack performs worst.

\ THE TOKENIZATION MARKET CASPER IS UNDERWRITING

The ERC-3643 standard the Manifest aligns with is no longer experimental. As of early 2026, ERC-3643 has been used to tokenize over $32 billion in real-world assets across more than 180 jurisdictions. Institutional adopters include DTCC, which integrated the standard into its ComposerX platform in March 2025, alongside Apex Group, Invesco, Franklin Templeton, and Fasanara Capital. The SEC Chairman cited it by name in a July 2025 speech. Singapore's Project Guardian under MAS is built on it. ISO standardisation is in progress.

\

\ The Manifest's positioning of Casper as "the first Layer 1 where regulatory compliance and transaction privacy are designed to work together" is a deliberate response to where ERC-3643 deployments currently break. Compliance enforcement at the token level means transactions are public by default, which works for traditional finance audit trails but conflicts with the privacy expectations of issuers handling sensitive instrument types. Casper's approach pairs ERC-3643 compliance logic with confidential transactions that auditors and regulators can verify without exposing details to the public chain. Privacy and compliance presented as two sides of the same system, not competing requirements.

\

The total addressable market is the figure that anchors the bet. Boston Consulting Group's frequently cited estimate puts tokenized real-world assets at $16 trillion by 2030. The current locked value sits at $12 to 25 billion depending on whose dashboard you use. The gap between today's footprint and the 2030 figure is roughly three orders of magnitude. The infrastructure that gets selected for the next phase of adoption is not selected on throughput. It is selected on compliance, jurisdictional coverage, and integration with existing financial plumbing.

\ THE MACHINE-ECONOMY POSITIONING

The X402 initiative is the more time-sensitive of the two big bets. The protocol, developed by Coinbase and Cloudflare and now governed by the X402 Foundation that includes Google and Visa, processed over 119 million transactions on Base and 35 million on Solana as of March 2026, with roughly $600 million in annualized volume and zero protocol fees. X402 V2 in December 2025 added reusable sessions, multi-chain support, and automatic service discovery, the features required for high-frequency multi-step agent workflows. Google's Agent Payments Protocol integrated X402 alongside cards and real-time bank transfers, explicitly listing stablecoins as a supported settlement type.

\

The category has reached the moment where standardization, not invention, is the constraint. Every agent framework that invents its own payment authorization logic creates a merchant integration problem that prevents scale. Casper's bet is to ship production X402 support at the Layer 1 level rather than as a smart-contract module, so AI agents holding native tokens or stablecoins on Casper can transact at API speed without a separate payment runtime. The Manifest's claim of becoming "the first WebAssembly-native Layer 1 with production X402 support" is specific enough to be falsifiable, which is rare in roadmap language.

\

\ THE QUANTUM CLAIM

The post-quantum signing initiative is the part of the Manifest that institutional buyers will read first, even if developers read it last. No major smart contract platform has shipped post-quantum transaction signing as of May 2026. Casper's commitment to hybrid accounts carrying both classical and quantum-resistant keys during a transition period gives institutions evaluating decade-long deployments a deliverable answer rather than a research citation.

\ For a sovereign wealth fund or a pension administrator running a 25-year tokenization horizon, the question of what happens when quantum computers can break elliptic-curve signatures is not abstract. The Manifest's answer is hybrid accounts shipping by 2027.

\ THE TIMELINE THAT MATTERS

The nine initiatives do not ship as a single release. The sequence published with the Manifest puts X402 micropayments first, in the coming weeks. EVM compatibility, networking hardening, and compliant security tokens follow later in 2026. The Native Token Registry, gasless transactions, batch operations, and smart accounts come after that. Transaction privacy and quantum safety build on the earlier work through 2027. Formal protocol enhancement proposals for each initiative will be published as they ship.

\ The sequencing is doing strategic work. X402 first is the move that creates the most immediate developer mindshare, because the AI agent payment narrative is the loudest demand signal in the category right now. EVM compatibility next is the move that opens the broadest contributor funnel. Compliant security tokens at the same window puts the institutional asset path in production within the same calendar year as the developer ramp. Quantum safety last is the move that lets the network claim a frontier technical position once the immediate adoption work is in place.

\ WHERE THE BET GETS DECIDED

The honest read on the Manifest is that it converts or it does not, and the conversion is decided in three different places on three different clocks.

\ The first ship is the credibility anchor. A roadmap with nine initiatives gets discounted on every miss; an opener that lands cleanly compounds in the opposite direction. The thing worth watching is not the X402 announcement itself but the first stablecoin treasury or agent-framework partner that routes visible volume across Casper inside the first quarter of operation. Quiet ships earn nothing. The names already moving in this category, Coinbase's AgentKit, the World protocol's human-verified agent payments, Cloudflare Workers, Cryptorefills on the merchant side, are the partners whose interest would signal that Casper is being read as an X402-native chain rather than an X402-late chain.

\

Then come the issuers, later in the year. EVM compatibility and compliant security tokens land in the same window, and the question worth tracking is which issuers select Casper over Ethereum given that Ethereum already hosts $32 billion in compliant assets and is the standard adopters know. The case Casper is making for that switch is the compliance-plus-privacy frame, and the specific buyer who finds it compelling will be the European or Asian wealth platform underwriting tokenized funds for high-net-worth investors. Those platforms have a quiet problem with public-chain ERC-3643 deployments. The same transfer history that satisfies the regulator exposes investor activity to anyone running a block explorer, which is unacceptable for the same investors the platforms most need. The first named Casper-native security token, and the jurisdiction it issues in, will tell us whether the positioning is being read correctly by the buyer it is built for.

\ The third place the bet gets decided is the slowest and the highest-stakes. Tier-1 financial market infrastructure players, DTCC, MAS, the BIS Innovation Hub, the Eurosystem digital euro pilots, move on their own clocks. Any one of them naming Casper in a regulated tokenization pilot would validate the multi-year thesis faster than the roadmap itself ships. The window worth watching is the second half of 2026, when these institutions typically commission their next round of pilots and when the calendar aligns with Casper's compliant security token release.

\ A network that delivers all three would not be the cheapest chain, the fastest chain, or the largest ecosystem. It would be the chain that the next trillion dollars in tokenized assets and the first billion machine-to-machine payments route through because the alternatives still treat compliance, privacy, and machine-readiness as competing requirements. The Manifest treats them as one specification, and that specification is what the roadmap is now committed to building.

\

title: Why the SEC Delayed Prediction Market ETFs
partialText: Prediction market ETFs cleared the standard SEC review window, then the regulator asked for more time. The real issue is structural: event contracts settle on interpreted outcomes, not objective data, which creates ambiguity the ETF wrapper concentrates rather than resolves. There's also a jurisdiction gap between the CFTC, which oversees the underlying platforms, and the SEC, which oversees the fund. Neither agency has worked out what happens when those frameworks collide during a contested resolution with retail money already in the fund. The delay is likely temporary, but the problems it surfaces are not.

title: Tokenizing TradFi’s $1.7 Trillion Private Credit Empire
partialText: Private credit has exploded into a $1.7–3.5 trillion market offering 8–12%+ yields, but suffers from opacity, illiquidity, and exclusivity. Blockchain tokenization (now >$25B in tokenized credit) adds real-time transparency, near-instant settlement, fractional ownership, and DeFi composability. Leaders like Figure ($17B+ HELOCs), Maple, and Centrifuge are scaling fast with institutional backing (BlackRock, Apollo, KKR). It doesn’t eliminate credit risk or bad underwriting — it just makes the same economics faster, more visible, and accessible to more investors. The trap evolves rather than disappears.

title: Vapi Raises $50M Led by Peak XV to Build the Default Infrastructure for Enterprise Voice AI
partialText:
\

What does enterprise customer service look like when most calls no longer have a human behind the phone?

\ Amazon Ring moved 100% of its inbound customer support volume onto AI voice agents and reported CSAT scores improved. Intuit, New York Life, ServiceTitan, Instawork, and Kavak are running production voice AI inside revenue-critical workflows. The American Customer Satisfaction Index has dropped two points since 2022 and has not meaningfully moved in nine years, even as enterprises poured hundreds of billions into chatbots, automation, and self-service portals. Roughly $3 trillion in global sales are projected to be at risk in 2026 because of bad customer experiences.

\ Vapi, the San Francisco voice AI platform announcing its Series B today, is built around a single bet. The bet is that the answer to the post-IVR question is not another conversational chatbot. It is an API-native infrastructure layer that produces production-grade voice agents in the specific shape of each enterprise's actual workflows, in days rather than months. Today the company announced a $50 million round led by Peak XV, with participation from M12, Microsoft's Venture Fund, Kleiner Perkins, Bessemer Venture Partners, and earlier investors, bringing total funding to $72 million.

\

\

THE TRILLION DOLLAR CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE CHANNEL IS BROKEN

Enterprise customer-experience spending has consumed a decade of investment without moving the score that matters. American CSAT, measured by ACSI, has been flat since 2017 and down two points since 2022. Most of the problem it was meant to solve remains unsolved. Across industries, customer service operations still run on a fragmented mix of rigid phone trees, brittle automation scripts, and contact-center workflows that were never designed to listen, adapt, or close a loop.

\ The reason is structural. IVR and chatbot platforms were built for the median customer interaction. Enterprise customer service is anything but median. Every company has its own escalation chain, its own compliance constraints, its own claims taxonomy, its own customer-segmentation logic. The standard solution has been to either bend the conversation around the platform's assumptions or pay a systems integrator to bridge the gap with custom development. Both options are expensive, both are slow, and both produce systems that age into the next round of technical debt.

\

THE AMAZON RING PLAYBOOK

The reason Vapi has credibility on this thesis is not the press release. It is what Amazon Ring documented through its production deployment. Ring moved 100% of inbound customer service onto Vapi-built voice agents in two weeks. CSAT scores improved. The deployment is not a chatbot. It is custom voice AI built into the specific shape of Ring's smart-home customer support workflow, tuned by Ring's own teams without engineering dependency.

\

Jason Mitura, Vice President of Software Development at Amazon Ring, explains,

\

After evaluating dozens of vendors, Vapi stood out. We went from zero to production in two weeks, and 100% of our inbound volume now runs through the Vapi. Most importantly, we've maintained our high bar of support for our customers and CSAT scores have improved. Vapi gives our teams the ability to tune the agent experience without depending on engineering. A lot of AI tools promise great outcomes, Vapi has delivered on them.

\ The Ring deployment is the public case. The broader pattern is less dramatic and more durable. Voice agents built into the specific shape of inbound claims, outbound collections, candidate screening, sales coaching, and autonomous IVR navigation outperform the off-the-shelf SaaS contact-center tools they replaced. They take days to deploy. They previously required engineering teams Amazon had and most companies do not.

\

WHY "ENTERPRISE VOICE INFRASTRUCTURE" IS A NEW BILLION DOLLAR CATEGORY

Vapi's positions itself as not a conversational chatbot or a contact-center SaaS replacement. It is not a low-code agent builder. The company describes itself as the API-native platform for building, deploying, and managing voice agents at scale, a framing that maps to a specific gap in the current AI tooling market.

\

\ Foundation voice models make speech in and speech out cheap. They do not produce production voice systems on their own. The vibe-coding tier of voice tools ships demos in hours, but the output is rarely the kind of thing a regulated enterprise routes 100% of inbound volume through. Traditional contact-center vendors produce production-grade systems, but take months and require enterprise sales cycles and integration teams most companies do not have. Vapi's claim is that AI now collapses the time and team size required to deploy production voice infrastructure, but only if the system around the model handles the latency optimization, model swapping, telephony abstraction, call-level observability, and governance that enterprise workloads actually demand.

\

The architecture is the unfair advantage. Without that layer, the output is just another voice demo. With it, the output is a production system that handles a billion calls.

\

THE PILOT NUMBERS

Vapi is already live with enterprise deployments across financial services, healthcare, insurance, automotive, and workforce management. Named customers include Amazon Ring, Kavak, Instawork, New York Life, UnityAI, Cherry, and Intuit. The disclosed results are concrete. Amazon Ring went from zero to production in two weeks. More than one million developers have built on the platform. Over 2.7 million unique agents have been created. Vapi's voice AI has handled more than one billion calls. Enterprise ARR has grown 10x in the past twelve months.

\

\

THE TAM AND THE PEAK XV THESIS

The market Vapi sits inside is not small. Conversational AI software is the fastest-growing sub-segment of the broader AI tooling stack, and enterprise voice AI is the fastest-growing sub-segment inside that. Total addressable customer-interaction spend approaches half a trillion dollars globally when contact-center labor, IVR infrastructure, telephony, and CRM voice modules are summed together. Voice agents are the first AI application with line-of-sight to all four of those budget lines simultaneously.

\

\ Peak XV's framing of the round reads as a deliberate distancing from the broader AI hype cycle. The reference companies named are not OpenAI or Anthropic. They are Zapier and n8n. The comparables named are not call-center incumbents. They are Supabase, PostHog, ClickHouse, and Better Auth. Both choices are deliberate.

\

\ The Zapier and n8n analogue places Vapi at the workflow-orchestration layer, not the model layer. The bet is that voice AI follows the same arc as integration tooling: foundation models become commodity inputs, the orchestration layer accrues switching costs, and the platform that owns developer mindshare at that layer captures the enterprise spend that follows. That is a materially different category to underwrite than "AI-enhanced contact center," and it prices differently.

\ The four portfolio comparables are the second half of the thesis. All four are bottom-up, developer-led infrastructure companies. The pattern across them is identical. Developers ship prototypes on the free tier. Prototypes become production. Production becomes the company-wide standard. Procurement signs the enterprise contract. CAC is near zero at the top of the funnel because the developer is the buyer. Gross margins compound as contract value steps up. Vapi is the first voice-AI bet placed inside that thesis, and the time-to-Series-B figures line up. ClickHouse closed its B at 18 months, Vapi at 34, Supabase at 36, PostHog at 40. The cohort runs on a recognizable clock.

\

\ The Amazon Ring case is the proof point that the motion scales. If a $300bn-market-cap parent organization can deploy through inbound self-serve in two weeks, the same path is available for every enterprise below it.

\

\ Co-founders Jordan Dearsley and Nikhil Gupta met at the University of Waterloo and previously built a Y Combinator-backed calendar app that reached profitability. Vapi itself started almost by accident. In mid-2023, Dearsley built a voice-based AI therapist for his daily walks, chaining models together and shaving latency until he had a working phone-based system. The therapy product did not take off. The latency stack underneath did. Vapi launched publicly on Product Hunt in March 2024. Twenty-six months later, more than one million developers have built on it.

\

WHAT TO WATCH

Three signals will determine whether Vapi defines the category or shares it.

\ The first is whether the developer-to-enterprise conversion curve holds. One million developers is a top-of-funnel number. The question is what fraction of that base produces multi-year enterprise contracts that survive procurement, security review, and regulatory due diligence. The Amazon Ring deployment is a strong public case. Twenty more of those convert the category.

\ The second is whether the API-native framing holds against competitive pressure from incumbents. The contact-center vendors, the telephony platforms, and the hyperscaler AI suites are not going to cede the operational voice layer without fighting for it. The obvious counter-move is bundling voice agent generation into existing contact-center products. Vapi's defense is the developer flywheel and the latency stack, both of which are harder to replicate than feature lists.

\ The third is whether voice agents take on the higher-stakes workflows where governance and predictability matter more than capability. Compliance-sensitive inbound, regulated outbound, and patient-facing healthcare are the workloads that will validate whether voice AI becomes the default enterprise interface or stays in the support-tier corner. Vapi has signaled its next investment cycle is in exactly that direction. Deeper reliability, stronger guardrails, clearer escalation paths to human operators. The Klarna and Pit playbook for one company. The Vapi playbook for every company that picks up the phone.

\ The bet is that in ten years, the phone tree is a museum piece and the AI agent is the default. The next four quarters will say whether the bet was early or late.
